title: Quiz: Reactions of Acids with Metals

questions.stem: What are the products when a reactive metal reacts with an acid?

options.text: A metal oxide and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: When a reactive metal reacts with an acid, the products are a salt and hydrogen gas: metal + acid → salt + hydrogen.

questions.stem: How do you test for hydrogen gas?

options.text: It produces a squeaky pop with a burning splint

questions.explanation: Hydrogen gas is tested by holding a burning splint near the gas. If hydrogen is present, it burns with a squeaky pop sound.

questions.stem: What salt is produced when magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen. The metal provides the first part of the salt name, and hydrochloric acid always produces chloride salts.

questions.stem: Why does copper NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid?

options.text: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from the acid

questions.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, meaning it is less reactive than hydrogen. Only metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen from acids.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals would react most vigorously with dilute sulfuric acid?
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than iron and copper, and gold does not react with dilute acids. Zinc is above hydrogen in the reactivity series and reacts vigorously, producing bubbles of hydrogen gas.

questions.stem: What would you observe when zinc is added to dilute hydrochloric acid?

options.text: The zinc dissolves and bubbles of gas are produced

questions.explanation: Zinc dissolves in the acid as it reacts, and bubbles of hydrogen gas are produced. The solution warms up slightly as the reaction is exothermic.

questions.stem: What salt is formed when iron reacts with sulfuric acid?
questions.explanation: Iron + sulfuric acid → iron sulfate + hydrogen. Sulfuric acid always produces sulfate salts in its reactions.
